approaches.name: Posterior triceps-elevating approach
approaches.corridor: Posterior exposure with subperiosteal reflection of the triceps-extensor sleeve from the olecranon toward the radial side

sources.title: Surgical approaches for ORIF of intra-articular distal humerus fractures in adults
Comparison of outcomes after triceps split versus sparing surgery for extra-articular distal humerus fractures

procedure_applications.condition: Extensile joint access is needed and a repairable triceps takedown is acceptable
Selected fractures require posterior access without an olecranon osteotomy

positioning.text: Position lateral or prone with the arm supported, the elbow freely flexed beyond 100 degrees, and the posterior humerus accessible for imaging.

setup.text: Plan ulnar-nerve management, triceps reattachment, postoperative extensor protection, and an alternative exposure if articular visualization is insufficient.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the distal humeral shaft, medial and lateral epicondyles, olecranon, subcutaneous ulna, and ulnar-nerve course.

incision.text: Use a posterior incision from the middle-distal humeral junction toward the ulnar diaphysis, curving around rather than directly over the olecranon tip.

superficial_interval.text: Raise full-thickness fasciocutaneous flaps and identify the ulnar nerve proximally, releasing it through the cubital tunnel to the first FCU motor branch while preserving perineural vessels.

deep_interval.text: Detach the triceps insertion and extensor apparatus subperiosteally, or with a thin olecranon bone wafer, then release anconeus and lateral extensor attachments so the sleeve reflects radially.

layers.text: Skin, full-thickness posterior flaps, ulnar-nerve plane, triceps-extensor insertion, posterior capsule, then distal-humeral joint.

structures_encountered.text: Ulnar nerve, triceps tendon, anconeus, lateral extensor origin, posterior capsule, olecranon, and distal humerus are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Ulnar nerve and FCU motor branch, radial nerve proximally, triceps insertion, collateral ligaments, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Do not place traction through a clipped ulnar-nerve sling; at closure the nerve must be tension free and separated from sutures and implants.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the reflected extensor sleeve as a broad unit and avoid focal traction on the ulnar nerve or excessive stripping from the proximal ulna.

exposure.text: Provides extensile posterior joint access useful for elbow arthroplasty while avoiding creation of an olecranon osteotomy.

limitations.text: The approach creates a triceps repair whose healing constrains rehabilitation and carries a risk of extensor insufficiency.

extensions.text: Release the posterior capsule and lateral extensor-anconeus attachments as needed; remove only the olecranon tip when additional flexion-based visualization is required.

indications.text: Use primarily for total elbow arthroplasty and selectively for distal-humerus reconstruction where triceps reflection is acceptable.

relative_contraindications.text: Prefer a triceps-sparing or transolecranon exposure when preservation of active extension or complete direct articular visualization is the dominant requirement.

implant_implications.text: Keep implants and repair sutures away from the final ulnar-nerve position and preserve olecranon bone adequate for transosseous triceps fixation.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, and oblique views to verify reconstruction and implant containment when visualization is incomplete.

closure.text: Reattach the triceps securely to olecranon with heavy nonabsorbable transosseous locking sutures and document the tension-free final ulnar-nerve position.

complications.text: Complications include triceps insufficiency, ulnar neuropathy, stiffness, infection, heterotopic ossification, nonunion, and implant failure.

bailouts.text: If safe articular visualization remains inadequate, convert deliberately to a transolecranon exposure rather than extending uncontrolled soft-tissue release.

questions.question: What is the defining maneuver?
questions.answer: Subperiosteal reflection of the triceps-extensor sleeve from the olecranon toward the radial side.

questions.question: What activity is restricted during healing?

approaches.name: Posterior triceps-splitting approach
approaches.corridor: Midline longitudinal split through triceps tendon, aponeurosis, and distal muscle with subperiosteal elevation from proximal ulna

sources.title: Surgical approaches for ORIF of intra-articular distal humerus fractures in adults
Comparison of outcomes after triceps split versus sparing surgery for extra-articular distal humerus fractures

procedure_applications.condition: An extra-articular fracture or open injury already splitting triceps requires broad posterior humeral exposure

positioning.text: Position lateral or prone with the arm supported, elbow freely flexed, and posterior humerus available for fluoroscopy.

setup.text: Define required proximal exposure, radial-nerve identification threshold, distal triceps-repair plan, and postoperative extension restrictions before incision.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the distal humeral shaft, olecranon, subcutaneous ulna, epicondyles, and expected radial- and ulnar-nerve courses.

incision.text: Use a posterior incision from the middle-distal humeral junction to the ulnar diaphysis, avoiding direct placement over the olecranon tip.

superficial_interval.text: Raise full-thickness fasciocutaneous flaps and expose the midline triceps fascia without undermining thin skin flaps.

deep_interval.text: Split the triceps tendon in the midline from olecranon tip to olecranon fossa, extend the split 3-4 cm proximal to the fracture, and elevate distal attachments subperiosteally from ulna.

layers.text: Skin, posterior flap, triceps fascia and tendon, distal triceps muscle, posterior periosteum, then distal humerus.

structures_encountered.text: Triceps tendon, aponeurosis and muscle, olecranon, posterior humeral cortex, and posterior capsule are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Radial nerve proximally, triceps insertion distally, ulnar nerve medially, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: If the split must extend farther proximally, identify and protect the radial nerve before advancing dissection.

retraction_hazards.text: Use smooth broad retractors and avoid forceful medial retraction toward the ulnar nerve or proximal retraction across the radial nerve.

exposure.text: Provides broad posterior exposure of the distal humeral columns and shaft through an extensile midline muscle split.

limitations.text: Direct visualization of the distal articular surface remains limited and the divided extensor mechanism requires secure repair and protection.

extensions.text: Extend proximally only after identifying the radial nerve; extend distally by careful subperiosteal release of triceps from proximal ulna.

indications.text: Use for extra-articular distal-humerus fixation and selected open fractures in which a traumatic triceps split can be incorporated for debridement and fixation.

relative_contraindications.text: Prefer a transolecranon exposure for complex complete-articular patterns requiring broad direct visualization and a triceps-sparing approach when extensor preservation is prioritized.

implant_implications.text: The corridor supports posterior and column fixation, but implants must not obstruct anatomic transosseous restoration of the distal triceps insertion.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, and oblique views to assess articular congruity and screw containment because direct articular visualization is limited.

closure.text: Close proximal muscle split with absorbable suture and reattach distal triceps to olecranon with heavy nonabsorbable transosseous sutures.

complications.text: Complications include triceps weakness or insufficiency, radial or ulnar neuropathy, stiffness, infection, heterotopic ossification, nonunion, and fixation failure.

bailouts.text: Convert to a more extensile articular exposure when reduction cannot be verified rather than lengthening the proximal split blindly.

questions.question: How far is the split normally extended beyond the fracture?
questions.answer: Approximately 3-4 cm proximal to the fracture line.

questions.question: What distal repair is essential?
questions.answer: Secure transosseous reattachment of triceps to olecranon.

approaches.name: Transolecranon approach to the distal humerus
approaches.corridor: Posterior transarticular exposure through a distally-apex chevron osteotomy at the olecranon bare area with triceps attached to the proximal fragment

sources.title: Surgical approaches for ORIF of intra-articular distal humerus fractures in adults
Outcomes for Type 13C1 and 13C2 fractures using the paratricipital approach

procedure_applications.condition: A complex intra-articular fracture requires maximal direct visualization of the distal-humeral articular surface

positioning.text: Position lateral or prone with arm supported, elbow freely flexed, and the posterior humerus accessible for fluoroscopy.

setup.text: Choose and preplan osteotomy fixation, confirm proximal-ulna suitability, plan ulnar-nerve management, and identify the intended bare-area osteotomy level before cutting.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark distal humeral shaft, epicondyles, olecranon, greater sigmoid notch, subcutaneous ulna, and ulnar-nerve course.

incision.text: Use a posterior incision from the middle-distal humeral junction toward the ulnar shaft, curving around rather than directly over olecranon tip.

superficial_interval.text: Raise full-thickness flaps; identify and release ulnar nerve through cubital tunnel to first FCU motor branch while preserving perineural vessels.

deep_interval.text: Reflect anconeus laterally and ulnar FCU head medially, mark a distally-apex chevron through the trochlear-notch bare area, saw only three quarters through bone, and complete with an osteotome.

layers.text: Skin, full-thickness flap, ulnar-nerve plane, anconeus and FCU margins, olecranon osteotomy, then distal-humeral articular surface.

structures_encountered.text: Ulnar nerve, triceps-olecranon unit, anconeus, FCU, greater sigmoid notch, posterior capsule, and distal-humeral joint are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Ulnar nerve and FCU motor branch, trochlear-notch cartilage, proximal-ulna cortex, triceps mechanism, and distal-humeral cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Aim through the narrow bare area, protect humeral cartilage, drill the chevron apex, and complete the subchondral bridge with an osteotome to avoid cartilage injury and fracture propagation.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the proximal olecranon-triceps fragment without levering on cartilage and avoid sustained traction on the mobilized ulnar nerve.

exposure.text: Provides the broadest direct visualization of the distal-humeral articular surface and both columns while preserving triceps attachment to the osteotomized fragment.

limitations.text: Adds an osteotomy that must unite and may produce symptomatic hardware requiring later removal.

extensions.text: Extend proximally along both columns after nerve identification while retaining the osteotomized olecranon-triceps unit as one sleeve.

indications.text: Use for complex intra-articular distal-humerus fractures when complete articular reduction requires direct visualization.

relative_contraindications.text: Prefer a triceps-sparing window for simpler C1-C2 or extra-articular patterns when adequate reduction is possible without osteotomy morbidity.

implant_implications.text: Predrill or template the intended osteotomy fixation before cutting; repair options include plate, intramedullary fixation, or cerclage-compression constructs.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, and oblique views to confirm distal-humerus reconstruction, olecranon reduction, implant position, and screw containment.

closure.text: Anatomically interdigitate and compress the chevron osteotomy with the planned construct, then leave the ulnar nerve tension free away from implants and document its final location.

complications.text: Complications include osteotomy nonunion or displacement, symptomatic hardware, ulnar neuropathy, stiffness, infection, heterotopic ossification, and fixation failure.

bailouts.text: If the osteotomy propagates or fixation purchase is poor, convert to stable plate fixation spanning adequate proximal-ulna bone rather than accepting an unstable repair.

questions.question: Where should the osteotomy cross the notch?
questions.answer: Through the bare area near the narrowest portion of the greater sigmoid notch.

questions.question: Why is a chevron preferred?
questions.answer: It improves exposure and gives inherent rotational stability with an interdigitating repair surface.

questions.question: How should the final subchondral bridge be completed?
questions.answer: With an osteotome after sawing only partway through the olecranon.
